svg.title: Pages: specs and docs that live beside the epics they describe — SoftTrack web design mockup (#281)
svg.desc: A ticket’s description is the only long text SoftTrack holds, so the specification behind an epic is in another tool behind a link. A page belongs to a team, is written in the editor tickets use, nests under other pages, links to epics and tickets both ways, keeps every save as a version, and is found by search.
svg.text: Pages: specs and docs that live beside the epics they describe
· the long text a ticket has no room for
A spec, beside the epic it describes

g.text: Engineering → Pages, signed in as Lena
Lena Fischer · edited 2 days ago · version 4
Why a link and not a password
Customers sign in a few times a year. A password they chose in January is one they have lost
by June, and support resets it by hand. See
The link works once and for fifteen minutes. It is built in
A second link retires the first
The link works once and for an hour.
The link works once and for fifteen minutes.
Why, what is built, what is not.
The question, the options, what was chosen.
Who was there, what was agreed, who does what.

svg.text: Done when a team can write pages in markdown with mentions, task lists, attachments and ticket keys that link themselves; pages nest into a tree; they link to epics and tickets
both ways; every save is a version that can be compared and restored; a page has comments and templates; search finds pages; and who sees a page follows the team, with
guests reading and external accounts reading only what is linked to an epic they were given.

g.text: task lists, attachments, and ticket keys that link
Pages nest, to make a tree.
Linked to epics and tickets, both
ways. Every save is a version.
Two people typing at once: the second to save is told the page
As it does for ticket descriptions.
Members write, guests read. Search finds pages and says which
